question: Four point charges sit at the corners of a square. A positive test charge is fixed at corner A. Without doing any calculation, which condition is SUFFICIENT to guarantee that the net electric force on the test charge at A points **exactly along the diagonal through A** (either toward or away from the square’s center), regardless of the value of the diagonally opposite corner’s charge?

options.A: The two charges adjacent to A have equal magnitude and the same sign (with each other); the diagonally opposite corner’s charge may be arbitrary.
options.B: The two charges adjacent to A have equal magnitude but opposite signs; the diagonally opposite charge must be zero.
options.C: All three other corner charges must be equal in magnitude and sign.
options.D: Only the diagonally opposite corner’s charge must equal the adjacent charges; the signs of the adjacent charges do not matter.
